meta.expansion: trinary (-1, 0, +1) non-parametric intelligence without LLMs, reasoning by derivation over explicit trinary substrate, shipping knowledge as portable .tarchi package
meta.archaion_meaning: Intelligence From The Beginning — derivation from foundational axioms rather than interpolation from a corpus
meta.meaning_of_true: Trinary truth values: -1 false, 0 unknown, +1 true, applied across multiple orthogonal layers (proposition, node, edge)

origin_context.prior_art_summary: Python prototype frozen as binary/float control group for A/B testing, bug at learning.py:211 fixed, will be upgraded to consume .tarchi packages

glossary.Tridak: Base-3 balanced digit {-1,0,+1}, atomic logical update unit for TArchI
glossary.Balradix: Numeral family: base-3 (Tridak) for atomic ops, odd bases only; balanced radix needs no sign bit, negates for free, single canonical zero
glossary.Baldec: 11-level ordinal score {-5..+5}, stored in 4 bits, used for strength graduation and promotion — not a positional radix-10 digit
glossary.Nubit: Unit of projection: one legal successor state with polarity, unsigned confidence, legality, rule_id, premise_ids, substitution
glossary.Astra: Portable knowledge artifact; capability measured by frozen two-suite vector (recall + derivation) against a documented 27B reference checkpoint
glossary.rubik_layer: Deterministic verifier: illegal states unrepresentable, independent proof checker
glossary.chess_layer: Bounded heuristic search over Nubit fan-out with explicit budgets; no opponent model, no shortest-path guarantee
glossary.curriculum: Knowledge acquisition pipeline: corpus -> template extraction -> canonicalization -> verification -> promotion -> decay(priority) -> graduation -> lossless schema factoring
glossary.substrate: Explicit trinary knowledge representation containing axioms, rules, and facts at multiple layers
glossary.four_trit_roles: Orthogonal trinary roles across layers: Truth (proposition), Polarity (edge), Epistemic (ledger), Balance (node charge)
glossary.node_27_states: Combinations of (truth, epistemic, balance) = 27 distinct semantic states; lifecycle is a derived classifier with external inputs
glossary.realizer: Trait adapter that constructs answers from resolved substrate plus ProofDAG for generation
glossary.tarchi_package: .tarchi format: knowledge package with 4KiB mmap-able pages, u64 page table, block codec, two-tier integrity, composable and delta-updatable

decisions.question: Should TArchI be a standalone project at /home/fola/tarchi or part of oracule-core rewrite?

options.label: Standalone
options.description: New project at /home/fola/tarchi, separate git repo

decisions.answer: Established TArchI as independent project at /home/fola/tarchi
decisions.rationale: Clean separation enables focused development and independent benchmarking from oracule-core prototype

decisions.question: How should trinary values be structured across different abstraction levels?

options.label: Three-layer approach
options.description: Truth at proposition, node triune, edge polarity levels

decisions.answer: Implemented three-level trinary layering simultaneously
decisions.rationale: Enables comprehensive knowledge representation across different abstraction levels

decisions.question: What are the fundamental trinary roles needed for comprehensive intelligence?

options.label: Four orthogonal roles
options.description: Truth, Polarity, Epistemic, Balance across different layers

decisions.answer: Defined four orthogonal trinary roles across four layers
decisions.rationale: Enables nuanced representation of truth, relationships, confidence, and stability
consequences: Deterministic lifecycle classifier with external inputs

decisions.question: Should TArchI be self-contained or a router to other models?

options.label: Complete stack
options.description: End-to-end intelligence from perception to action

decisions.answer: Built complete self-contained intelligence stack
decisions.rationale: No external dependencies, full autonomy, enables unique capabilities and benchmarking
decisions.note: v0.1 delivers read-only resolve/explain/cite; act/induction deferred

decisions.question: How should intelligence be derived — from axioms or from data?

options.label: Axiomatic derivation with premise qualification
options.description: From foundational axioms and logical derivation; empirical claims are source-qualified

decisions.answer: Adopted Archaion: checked entailment conditional on explicit trusted premises; empirical observations are attributed, not established as universal truth
decisions.rationale: Ensures traceable, verifiable reasoning; axiom consistency cannot establish empirical truth

decisions.question: How should development scope be managed — fixed upfront or staged?

options.label: Staged milestones with early device gate
options.description: M0-M7 with device feasibility before M5, M0 reopened for contract repair

decisions.answer: Implemented staged development with M0-M7 milestones; M0 reopened for contract repair; device feasibility moved before M5
decisions.rationale: Manageable development with regular validation; pivotal risks (device, density, soundness) gated early

decisions.question: What runtime and language should power TArchI?
decisions.answer: Rust core with Python research bindings
decisions.rationale: Rust provides no_std, SIMD, Android NDK, WASM targets; Python enables research while maintaining performance constraints

decisions.question: What numeral system should power TArchI arithmetic?

options.label: Balanced radix (odd bases only) + 11-level Baldec score
options.description: Tridak (base-3) for atomic ops; Baldec as scalar score, not positional radix-10

decisions.answer: Adopted Balradix family: Tridak (base-3 balanced digits {-1,0,+1}) for atomic operations; Baldec as 11-level ordinal score in 4 bits. Base-10 {-5..+5} is not a canonical positional digit set.
decisions.rationale: Eliminates sign bits, enables efficient negation, canonical zero; Baldec is a scalar, not positional arithmetic

decisions.question: What reference implementation should TArchI use for A/B testing?

options.label: Same-Rust codec ablation
options.description: i8/enum, 2-bit packed, dense base-3, dictionary/delta on identical workloads

options.label: Fixed oracule-core only
options.description: Python prototype conflates too many variables

decisions.answer: Use oracule-core as historical regression oracle. Causal trit-vs-bit comparison via same-Rust engine with four storage codecs on identical workloads.
decisions.rationale: Python-to-Rust comparison conflates language, allocator, object model, algorithms, paging, compression, and semantics. Same-runtime ablation isolates representation effect.

decisions.question: How should answers be generated without LLMs?

options.label: Constructive reasoning from ProofDAG
options.description: Realizer trait adapter from substrate + derivation

decisions.answer: Constructive generation via Realizer trait adapter from ProofDAG with sentence-level provenance
decisions.rationale: No LLMs anywhere in system, ensures precise, factual, cited responses; no-LLM does not forbid explicitly approved classical classifier

decisions.question: How should knowledge be acquired and maintained?

options.label: Curriculum pipeline with dependency-aware correction
options.description: Corpus -> extraction -> verification -> induction -> promotion -> decay(priority) -> graduation -> lossless factoring

decisions.answer: Curriculum-driven knowledge acquisition with versioned snapshots, reverse dependencies, decay on priority only, and lossless schema factoring in v0.1
decisions.rationale: No neural network training; continuous GPU-free learning; single-fact correction via dependency invalidation; verifiable facts only
decisions.supersedes: original D11 one-node-cost and no-forgetting guarantees

decisions.question: What scope should v0.1 target for initial release?

options.label: Closed-domain
options.description: RESOLVE + EXPLAIN + CITE over curated domains

decisions.answer: v0.1 scope: closed-domain question answering with RESOLVE (find answers), EXPLAIN (provide ProofDAG), and CITE (reference sources) capabilities over a curated set of domains
decisions.rationale: Comparable to binary control, high precision requirement, smaller initial implementation, clear evaluation metrics

decisions.question: What schema induction should v0.1 include?

options.label: Lossless factoring only
options.description: Supplied/reviewed schemas + lossless factoring; mined rules as hypotheses

decisions.answer: v0.1 ships with lossless schema factoring and supplied/reviewed schemas only. Induced rules are hypotheses with versioned evidence until independently accepted on held-out compositions. Full ILP deferred to M7. 10x target is falsifiable hypothesis.
decisions.rationale: Schema compression measured, not assumed; lossless factoring ≠ inductive generalization; three examples cannot prove universal rule

decisions.question: What knowledge source should v0.1 use?
decisions.answer: v0.1 knowledge: curated corpus + ground truth
decisions.rationale: Measurable extraction quality and citation coverage, high-quality initial facts

decisions.question: What format should knowledge packaging use?

options.label: .tarchi with block codec and lazy verification
options.description: 4KiB pages, u64 page table, block codec with restart points, lazy proof checks, authenticated manifest

decisions.answer: .tarchi package: memory-mapped 4 KiB pages with u64 page table, block codec with restart points, two-tier integrity (hash + lazy semantic proof checks keyed to immutable snapshot hashes), composable namespaced immutable assertions with deterministic resolution, delta-updatable via logical record deltas with atomic manifest
decisions.rationale: Efficient memory usage; lazy verification avoids 55-minute eager scan; authenticated manifest prevents self-reference; deterministic merge with evidence preservation
decisions.supersedes: original D15 trit-granular residency, eager verify, merge policy, sub-byte header

decisions.question: How should 1 Astra be defined?

options.label: Capability vector (no additive equivalence)
options.description: Recall, derivation, abstention, contradiction, bytes, latency vs frozen 27B reference

decisions.answer: 1 Astra = portable artifact measured by frozen two-suite capability vector against documented 27B reference. No additive parameter equivalence. 3.7 Astra does not mean 3.7× capability.
decisions.rationale: Parameter count ≠ capability; duplicate packages add zero coverage; 90% ceiling cannot multiply to 333%; database+recursive query can genuinely derive

decisions.question: What efficiency targets should TArchI achieve?

options.label: Measured whole-artifact + provisional app budget
options.description: 2 GB device constraint; ≤512 MiB app budget; 5 GB artifact as falsifiable target

decisions.answer: Retain 2 GB device as acceptance constraint. Provisional app budget: 512 MiB. 5 GB artifact target retained as falsifiable aspiration pending compression evidence. Move device feasibility gate before M5.
decisions.rationale: Sample projects ~25 GB at 3.3B facts; 1.8 GB allocation leaves ~200 MB for OS on literal 2 GB phone; 390K pinned pages exceed 1.6 GB
consequences: Smaller cache may increase page faults
decisions.supersedes: original D17 allocation model and 10x derivation

decisions.question: How should TArchI be validated?

options.label: Native + same-Rust codec ablation + frozen benchmark manifest
options.description: TArchI metrics plus causal trit-vs-bit on identical code paths; protocol registered before test

decisions.answer: Validate using TArchI-native metrics: state density, knowledge density (whole-artifact), latency, correctness, contradiction detection/correction, citation coverage, unsupported-claim rate, device footprint, and capability vector. Causal A/B via same-Rust codec ablation on identical workloads with frozen formulas.
decisions.rationale: Comprehensive validation with causal comparison capability; multiple quality dimensions; protocol prevents post-hoc metric changes

decisions.question: How should reasoning and planning be structured?

options.label: Independent proof checker + bounded heuristic search
options.description: Rubik = deterministic verifier; Chess = best-first search with explicit budgets and resource-limit outcomes

decisions.answer: Two layers: Rubik (independent proof checker, deterministic verification) and Chess (bounded heuristic search with explicit budgets: 100K apps, 64 MiB frontier, 2s). Proof DAG with premise IDs, substitution, snapshot hash. No universal truth, adversarial, or shortest-path guarantee by analogy.
decisions.rationale: Deterministic verification + bounded search; sound verification kernel; resource limits explicit to callers; De Morgan example invalid

decisions.question: How should perception work without LLMs?

options.label: Controlled-language grammar + deterministic templates
options.description: Lexer → morphology → lexicon → constraint parser → semantic extraction with source qualification

decisions.answer: Classical NLP pipeline with controlled language, deterministic templates, source-qualified empirical assertions, exact source spans, held-out negation/quantifier/unit/alias cases. Classical classifier only if explicitly approved. Language servers for code ground truth. Vision/audio out of scope v0.1.
decisions.rationale: Precise extraction with verifiable results; deterministic errors are still errors; no-LLM is narrower than no-ML; unsupported input remains unsupported

technical_facts.implication: Balanced ternary achieves 1.585 bits per trit theoretical; integer packing realizes up to 1.667 bits/trit

technical_facts.fact: Rubik's cube 4.3252e19 states = 66 bits vs 42 trits
technical_facts.implication: Trinary representation reduces state count vs binary by 1.57x (66/42)
Trinary chess representation saves 1.58x storage vs binary (149/94)

technical_facts.fact: 5 trits = 243 states fit in 1 byte (8 bits)
technical_facts.implication: Sub-byte dense addressing: 5 trits per byte, not 8 trits
8 trits cannot fit in 1 byte; 13 bits required, contradicting earlier claim
Classical template extraction achieved high precision without neural nets on specific corpus; not a guaranteed pipeline error rate for TArchI

technical_facts.fact: OWL 2 open-world semantics uses open-world assumption, not Kleene three-valued logic
technical_facts.implication: OWL's non-entailment is not the same as Kleene unknown; P∨¬P is true in every OWL interpretation, while Kleene unknown makes it unknown
Inductive logic programming enables rule induction from data; but three examples cannot prove a universal rule

technical_facts.fact: LLM marginal storage ~10-15 bytes per fact (unverified baseline)
technical_facts.implication: No common fact definition or measurement boundary established; not a committed TArchI baseline
Bug fix provides immediate improvement in control group; status unverified in its repo

technical_facts.implication: Development environment supports current architecture choices; device access required for M6

honest_limits: Traded open-domain recall and fuzzy similarity for verifiability/density/updateability/footprint (right trade for a 2 GB phone: you cannot ship a corpus but you can ship a compressed, verified, paged theory)
LLM weights carry implicit generalities no fact table expresses, so the density advantage holds for schema-heavy curated verified knowledge only
Without an LLM realizer the language is precise and cited but not charming
Extraction recall on prose is the weakest link
If derivation parity against a 27B reference fails, report absolute scores; do not rename baseline performance into a radix breakthrough
Axiom consistency cannot establish empirical truth; a false but consistent premise survives all checks
10x storage reduction is a falsifiable target pending matched-capability evidence, not an established property
